title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
shortDescription: The DPF is not trapping particulate matter as efficiently as required.
fullDescription: The PCM has detected that the diesel particulate filter on bank 1 is not capturing soot at the efficiency the manufacturer specifies. This is typically determined by comparing pressure differential across the DPF or by exhaust soot sensor data. A failed regeneration cycle or a damaged substrate is the most common cause.
safetyImpact: Aftertreatment faults can lead to limp-mode derate at highway speeds, which may surprise the driver in traffic.

causes.cause: Excessive soot loading from short-trip driving (no completed regeneration)
Failed or contaminated DPF / SCR substrate
Faulty exhaust gas temperature or DEF temperature sensor
DEF (urea) of incorrect quality or contaminated
Wiring or connector corrosion in aftertreatment harness
Failed reductant (DEF) pump or injector

symptoms: Check Engine Light / DEF warning lamp illuminated
Reduced engine power (limp mode) when threshold exceeded
Frequent or interrupted DPF regeneration cycles
Increased fuel consumption on diesel engines
Countdown to no-start in heavy-duty applications

fixSteps.title: Read freeze frame and live data
fixSteps.instruction: Use a bidirectional scan tool to read DPF soot mass, EGT temperatures, DEF tank level/quality, and SCR NOx efficiency. Review freeze frame for the conditions when the fault set.

fixSteps.title: Inspect aftertreatment harness and sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect EGT sensors, differential pressure hoses, NOx sensors, and the DEF tank heater connector. Look for chafe, oil contamination, and corrosion. Test sensor resistance against spec.

fixSteps.title: Attempt forced regeneration
fixSteps.instruction: If soot mass is high but below the no-regen threshold, command a stationary forced regeneration with the scan tool and observe EGT temperatures rise to the target window.

fixSteps.title: Inspect or replace DPF/SCR component
fixSteps.instruction: If pressure differential remains out of range or DEF dosing cannot recover SCR efficiency, remove the DPF for cleaning/baking or replace the SCR catalyst per OEM procedure.

faq.q: Can I keep driving with this code?
faq.a: Short distance is usually possible, but most diesels will derate power and may eventually refuse to start. Address aftertreatment faults promptly to avoid expensive component damage.

faq.q: Is forced regeneration safe to do myself?
faq.a: Forced regen produces very high exhaust temperatures and should only be performed in a controlled outdoor area away from flammable material, ideally with a professional scan tool.

faq.q: Will adding a DPF delete fix this?
faq.a: DPF deletes are illegal on road-going vehicles in the US, Canada, EU, and most jurisdictions. They also carry heavy fines and disable emissions warranty coverage.

fullDescription: The pump is responding to commands but flow or pressure feedback is outside expected limits. May be the early stage of pump failure or a clogged DEF filter.
safetyImpact: Aftertreatment faults can lead to limp-mode derate at highway speeds, which may surprise the driver in traffic.

causes.cause: Excessive soot loading from short-trip driving (no completed regeneration)
Failed or contaminated DPF / SCR substrate
Faulty exhaust gas temperature or DEF temperature sensor
DEF (urea) of incorrect quality or contaminated
Wiring or connector corrosion in aftertreatment harness
Failed reductant (DEF) pump or injector

symptoms: Check Engine Light / DEF warning lamp illuminated
Reduced engine power (limp mode) when threshold exceeded
Frequent or interrupted DPF regeneration cycles
Increased fuel consumption on diesel engines
Countdown to no-start in heavy-duty applications

fixSteps.title: Read freeze frame and live data
fixSteps.instruction: Use a bidirectional scan tool to read DPF soot mass, EGT temperatures, DEF tank level/quality, and SCR NOx efficiency. Review freeze frame for the conditions when the fault set.

fixSteps.title: Inspect aftertreatment harness and sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect EGT sensors, differential pressure hoses, NOx sensors, and the DEF tank heater connector. Look for chafe, oil contamination, and corrosion. Test sensor resistance against spec.

fixSteps.title: Attempt forced regeneration
fixSteps.instruction: If soot mass is high but below the no-regen threshold, command a stationary forced regeneration with the scan tool and observe EGT temperatures rise to the target window.

fixSteps.title: Inspect or replace DPF/SCR component
fixSteps.instruction: If pressure differential remains out of range or DEF dosing cannot recover SCR efficiency, remove the DPF for cleaning/baking or replace the SCR catalyst per OEM procedure.

faq.q: Can I keep driving with this code?
faq.a: Short distance is usually possible, but most diesels will derate power and may eventually refuse to start. Address aftertreatment faults promptly to avoid expensive component damage.

faq.q: Is forced regeneration safe to do myself?
faq.a: Forced regen produces very high exhaust temperatures and should only be performed in a controlled outdoor area away from flammable material, ideally with a professional scan tool.

faq.q: Will adding a DPF delete fix this?
faq.a: DPF deletes are illegal on road-going vehicles in the US, Canada, EU, and most jurisdictions. They also carry heavy fines and disable emissions warranty coverage.
